title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-3
notes:
West leads the ♠10 against 6NT. South has only 8 top tricks (3 spades, 3 hearts, and 2 clubs). The ♦K can knock out the ♦A and establish the ♦Q as trick 9. The other 3 tricks can be taken in clubs if the ♣Q can be picked up.

There are two alternatives to consider in playing the club suit. South can cash the ♣A and ♣K hoping clubs are 2-2 as above. This play will also work when either West or East has a singleton ♣Q and when East has all 4 clubs. In the latter case, West will show out on the first top club and South can finesse East out of his known ♣Q by leading through him twice from the North hand.

The alternative play is to finesse East for the ♣Q after cashing one top honour. This line of play gains over the first one when East has 3 clubs to the Queen, but loses to West's Queen doubleton of clubs.

The mathematics of all of these possibilities favours cashing the top honours. That is, cashing the ♣A and ♣K is slightly more likely to work than taking the second round finesse.

A famous bridge saying can be used to help you remember this play. "8 ever, 9 never" means that if North and South have 8 cards in a suit missing only the Queen, it is correct to finesse for the Queen. With 9 cards between the 2 hands, as above, it is correct to play for the drop.
